tagline: Data-driven, insight-led advisory, broking and solutions across people, risk and capital
hero_kpi_rationale: Operating margin expanding to 23% in 2025 (vs 6% in 2024), reflecting significant improvement in operational efficiency following post-transformation normalization

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue
kpis.description: Operating margin improves significantly to 23.0% in 2025 compared to 6.3% in 2024, reflecting the absence of major impairment charges and normalization following restructuring
kpis.signal: Significant expansion driven by the conclusion of transformation costs and improved efficiency

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of services (excluding overhead), divided by revenue
kpis.description: Gross margin of 73% (revenue less direct service costs) reflects stable management of operating expenses despite a 2% increase in salaries
kpis.signal: Relative stability despite wage pressures and efficiency gains

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total amount earned by the company during the fiscal year
kpis.description: Revenue of $9.7 billion in 2025 declines by 2.2% from $9.9 billion in 2024, impacted by softening market conditions and the divestiture of the TRANZACT business
kpis.signal: Slight decline reflecting softening insurance market and the sale of TRANZACT

kpis.name: Total Headcount (thousands)
kpis.description: Headcount remains stable at approximately 47,000 employees, reflecting maintained capacity following the sale of TRANZACT, offset by targeted hiring
kpis.signal: Stable workforce despite the divestiture of TRANZACT and selective growth

kpis.name: Salaries and Benefits (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Expenses for salaries and benefits as a percentage of total revenue
kpis.description: Salaries and benefits increase to 58% of revenue in 2025 (vs 55% in 2024), reflecting a 2% rise due to cost-of-living adjustments and inflationary pressures
kpis.signal: Increased pressure from wage costs due to inflation and compensation adjustments

kpis.name: AI-Enabled Contract Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new contracts and expansions incorporating artificial intelligence and advanced analytics capabilities
kpis.description: The proportion of deals including AI features rises to 18%, driven by growing demand for advanced analytics tools and technology solutions
kpis.signal: Accelerating client adoption of AI solutions, reflecting broader market technology trends

kpis.name: Annual Recurring Revenue (subscriptions and services)
kpis.explanation: Revenue from recurring contracts, subscriptions, and long-term service agreements
kpis.description: Recurring revenue grows to $4.1 billion (+6.5%), demonstrating successful expansion of digital platforms and subscription-based solutions despite softening market conditions
kpis.signal: Strong growth in recurring revenue, reflecting customer retention and transition to subscription models

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury).
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + share buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of 9.708 Bn USD in the last fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of 1.605 Bn USD in the last fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.description: Operating income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Operating income of 2.234 Bn USD in the last fiscal year (FY2025).

risks.title: Impact of currency fluctuations on revenues
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly states that currency fluctuations can materially impact revenues. The impact is quantified for 2025, indicating notable sensitivity. This risk is recurring in international operations.

risks.title: Risk related to business divestitures (TRANZACT)
risks.score_rationale: The sale of the TRANZACT business resulted in significant impairment charges in 2024 and affected comparative revenues. The repeated mention of this transaction and its financial consequences suggests a significant risk related to divestments.

risks.title: Increasing salary and benefits costs
risks.score_rationale: Salaries and benefits represent the largest cost component (58% in 2025). A 2% increase is noted, primarily due to cost-of-living adjustments. This weighs on profitability.

risks.title: Risks related to transformation and restructuring programs
risks.score_rationale: Restructuring, transaction, and transformation costs are mentioned, although declining after the completion of the transformation program in 2024. These programs involve significant costs and execution risks.

risks.title: Impact of international tax regulations (Pillar Two)
risks.score_rationale: The document references OECD rules on international taxation (Pillar Two) and their potential impact. While current rules do not appear to affect the company, evolving regulatory frameworks represent a risk.

risks.title: Dependence on advisory and broking services
risks.score_rationale: The majority of revenue comes from broking commissions and advisory fees. While no single client is significant, the nature of these services makes them sensitive to economic cycles and competition.

risks.title: Softening market conditions in insurance
risks.score_rationale: At the time of filing, documentation indicates a softening market, which exerts downward pressure on broking commission revenues and affects operating margins.

ai_positioning.summary: While WTW does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K, the company demonstrates an implicit positioning through investments in analytical, technological, and data-driven solutions. The 18% growth in contracts including AI features indicates progressive integration of AI capabilities into the client offering, particularly through advanced analytics tools and digital platforms.
evidence: Investments in analytical tools and technology solutions mentioned in MD&A
18% of deals include AI features (story KPI)
Transition to digital solutions and subscriptions ($4.1 billion ARR)
